4: 	"context"
5: 	"errors"

16: 
17: const (
18: 	ModeOff           Mode = "off"
19: 	ModeCommit        Mode = "commit"
20: 	ModeCommitAndPush Mode = "commit-and-push"
21: )
22: 
23: type Policy struct {
24: 	Mode        Mode
25: 	Remote      string
26: 	PushTimeout time.Duration
27: }
28: 
29: type Request struct {
30: 	Root     string
31: 	Paths    []string
32: 	All      bool
33: 	Message  string
34: 	Identity string
35: }
36: 
37: type Result struct {
38: 	Repository string `json:"repository"`
39: 	Branch     string `json:"branch"`
40: 	Commit     string `json:"commit,omitempty"`
41: 	Remote     string `json:"remote,omitempty"`
42: 	Committed  bool   `json:"committed"`
43: 	Pushed     bool   `json:"pushed"`
44: 	Skipped    bool   `json:"skipped"`
45: }
46: 
47: type Publisher interface {
48: 	Publish(context.Context, Request) (Result, error)
49: }
50: 
51: type CommandPublisher struct {
52: 	policy Policy
53: }
54: 
55: func New(policy Policy) CommandPublisher {
56: 	if policy.Mode == "" {
57: 		policy.Mode = ModeOff
58: 	}
59: 	if strings.TrimSpace(policy.Remote) == "" {
60: 		policy.Remote = "origin"
61: 	}
62: 	if policy.PushTimeout <= 0 {
63: 		policy.PushTimeout = 2 * time.Minute
64: 	}
65: 	return CommandPublisher{policy: policy}
66: }
67: 
68: func (p CommandPublisher) Publish(ctx context.Context, req Request) (Result, error) {
69: 	if p.policy.Mode == ModeOff {
70: 		return Result{Skipped: true}, nil
71: 	}
72: 	if ctx == nil {
73: 		ctx = context.Background()
74: 	}
75: 	root := filepath.Clean(strings.TrimSpace(req.Root))
76: 	if root == "" || root == "." {
77: 		return Result{}, fmt.Errorf("git publish: repository root is required")
78: 	}
79: 	repo, err := gitOutput(ctx, root, nil, "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel")
80: 	if err != nil {
81: 		return Result{}, fmt.Errorf("git publish: resolve repository from %s: %w", root, err)
82: 	}
83: 	repo, err = filepath.Abs(strings.TrimSpace(repo))
84: 	if err != nil {
85: 		return Result{}, fmt.Errorf("git publish: resolve repository path: %w", err)
86: 	}
87: 	branch, err := gitOutput(ctx, repo, nil, "branch", "--show-current")
88: 	if err != nil {
89: 		return Result{}, fmt.Errorf("git publish: resolve branch: %w", err)
90: 	}
91: 	branch = strings.TrimSpace(branch)
92: 	if branch == "" {
93: 		return Result{}, fmt.Errorf("git publish: detached HEAD is not supported")
94: 	}
95: 	result := Result{Repository: repo, Branch: branch}
96: 	paths, err := publishPaths(repo, req.Paths, req.All)
97: 	if err != nil {
98: 		return result, err
99: 	}
100: 	common, err := gitOutput(ctx, repo, nil, "rev-parse", "--git-common-dir")
101: 	if err != nil {
102: 		return result, fmt.Errorf("git publish: resolve common directory: %w", err)
103: 	}
104: 	common = strings.TrimSpace(common)
105: 	if !filepath.IsAbs(common) {
106: 		common = filepath.Join(repo, common)
107: 	}
108: 	common, err = filepath.Abs(filepath.Clean(common))
109: 	if err != nil {
110: 		return result, fmt.Errorf("git publish: resolve common directory path: %w", err)
111: 	}
112: 	lock, err := acquireLock(ctx, filepath.Join(common, "ultraplan-publish.lock"))
113: 	if err != nil {
114: 		return result, fmt.Errorf("git publish: acquire repository lock: %w", err)
115: 	}
116: 	defer lock.release()
117: 
118: 	if len(paths) > 0 {
119: 		commit, committed, commitErr := commitPaths(ctx, repo, common, paths, req.Message, req.Identity)
120: 		result.Commit, result.Committed = commit, committed
121: 		if commitErr != nil {
122: 			return result, commitErr
123: 		}
124: 	}
125: 	if result.Commit == "" {
126: 		result.Commit, err = gitOutput(ctx, repo, nil, "rev-parse", "HEAD")
127: 		if err != nil {
128: 			return result, fmt.Errorf("git publish: resolve HEAD: %w", err)
129: 		}
130: 		result.Commit = strings.TrimSpace(result.Commit)
131: 	}
132: 	if p.policy.Mode != ModeCommitAndPush {
133: 		return result, nil
134: 	}
135: 	if !validRemoteName(p.policy.Remote) {
136: 		return result, fmt.Errorf("git publish: invalid remote name %q", p.policy.Remote)
137: 	}
138: 	pushCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, p.policy.PushTimeout)
139: 	defer cancel()
140: 	upstreamRemote, upstreamErr := gitOutput(pushCtx, repo, nil, "for-each-ref", "--format=%(upstream:remotename)", "refs/heads/"+branch)
141: 	if upstreamErr != nil {
142: 		return result, fmt.Errorf("git publish: resolve upstream: %w", upstreamErr)
143: 	}
144: 	upstreamRemote = strings.TrimSpace(upstreamRemote)
145: 	if upstreamRemote != "" {
146: 		if !validRemoteName(upstreamRemote) {
147: 			return result, fmt.Errorf("git publish: invalid upstream remote name %q", upstreamRemote)
148: 		}
149: 		upstreamRef, refErr := gitOutput(pushCtx, repo, nil, "for-each-ref", "--format=%(upstream:remoteref)", "refs/heads/"+branch)
150: 		if refErr != nil || strings.TrimSpace(upstreamRef) == "" {
151: 			return result, fmt.Errorf("git publish: resolve upstream ref: %w", refErr)
152: 		}
153: 		result.Remote = upstreamRemote
154: 		_, err = gitOutput(pushCtx, repo, nil, "push", "--porcelain", "--", upstreamRemote, "HEAD:"+strings.TrimSpace(upstreamRef))
155: 	} else {
156: 		result.Remote = p.policy.Remote
157: 		_, err = gitOutput(pushCtx, repo, nil, "push", "--porcelain", "--set-upstream", "--", p.policy.Remote, "HEAD:refs/heads/"+branch)
158: 	}
159: 	if err != nil {
160: 		if errors.Is(pushCtx.Err(), context.DeadlineExceeded) {
161: 			return result, fmt.Errorf("git publish: push timed out after %s: %w", p.policy.PushTimeout, pushCtx.Err())
162: 		}
163: 		return result, fmt.Errorf("git publish: push %s/%s: %w", result.Remote, branch, err)
164: 	}
165: 	result.Pushed = true
166: 	return result, nil
167: }
168: 
169: func publishPaths(repo string, requested []string, all bool) ([]string, error) {
170: 	if all {
171: 		return []string{"."}, nil
172: 	}
173: 	set := map[string]bool{}
174: 	for _, raw := range requested {
175: 		if strings.TrimSpace(raw) == "" {
176: 			continue
177: 		}
178: 		path := filepath.Clean(raw)
179: 		if !filepath.IsAbs(path) {
180: 			path = filepath.Join(repo, path)
181: 		}
182: 		path, err := filepath.Abs(path)
183: 		if err != nil {
184: 			return nil, fmt.Errorf("git publish: resolve path %q: %w", raw, err)
185: 		}
186: 		rel, err := filepath.Rel(repo, path)
187: 		if err != nil || rel == ".." || strings.HasPrefix(rel, ".."+string(filepath.Separator)) {
188: 			return nil, fmt.Errorf("git publish: path %q escapes repository %s", raw, repo)
189: 		}
190: 		set[filepath.ToSlash(rel)] = true
191: 	}
192: 	paths := make([]string, 0, len(set))
193: 	for path := range set {
194: 		paths = append(paths, path)
195: 	}
196: 	sort.Strings(paths)
197: 	return paths, nil
198: }
199: 
200: func commitPaths(ctx context.Context, repo, common string, paths []string, message, identity string) (string, bool, error) {
201: 	message = strings.TrimSpace(message)
202: 	if message == "" {
203: 		return "", false, fmt.Errorf("git publish: commit message is required")
204: 	}
205: 	if identity != "" {
206: 		message += "\n\nUltraPlan-Publication: " + strings.TrimSpace(identity)
207: 	}
208: 	parent, err := gitOutput(ctx, repo, nil, "rev-parse", "HEAD")
209: 	if err != nil {
210: 		return "", false, fmt.Errorf("git publish: resolve commit parent: %w", err)
211: 	}
212: 	parent = strings.TrimSpace(parent)
213: 	temp, err := os.CreateTemp(common, "ultraplan-index-*")
214: 	if err != nil {
215: 		return "", false, fmt.Errorf("git publish: create temporary index: %w", err)
216: 	}
217: 	indexPath := temp.Name()
218: 	if closeErr := temp.Close(); closeErr != nil {
219: 		_ = os.Remove(indexPath)
220: 		return "", false, fmt.Errorf("git publish: close temporary index: %w", closeErr)
221: 	}
222: 	_ = os.Remove(indexPath)
223: 	defer os.Remove(indexPath)
224: 	env := []string{"GIT_INDEX_FILE=" + indexPath}
225: 	if _, err := gitOutput(ctx, repo, env, "read-tree", parent); err != nil {
226: 		return "", false, fmt.Errorf("git publish: seed temporary index: %w", err)
227: 	}
228: 	args := append([]string{"add", "-A", "--"}, paths...)
229: 	if _, err := gitOutput(ctx, repo, env, args...); err != nil {
230: 		return "", false, fmt.Errorf("git publish: stage owned paths: %w", err)
231: 	}
232: 	tree, err := gitOutput(ctx, repo, env, "write-tree")
233: 	if err != nil {
234: 		return "", false, fmt.Errorf("git publish: write tree: %w", err)
235: 	}
236: 	tree = strings.TrimSpace(tree)
237: 	parentTree, err := gitOutput(ctx, repo, nil, "rev-parse", parent+"^{tree}")
238: 	if err != nil {
239: 		return "", false, fmt.Errorf("git publish: resolve parent tree: %w", err)
240: 	}
241: 	if tree == strings.TrimSpace(parentTree) {
242: 		return parent, false, nil
243: 	}
244: 	commit, err := gitInput(ctx, repo, env, message+"\n", "commit-tree", tree, "-p", parent)
245: 	if err != nil {
246: 		return "", false, fmt.Errorf("git publish: create commit: %w", err)
247: 	}
248: 	commit = strings.TrimSpace(commit)
249: 	ref, err := gitOutput(ctx, repo, nil, "symbolic-ref", "-q", "HEAD")
250: 	if err != nil || strings.TrimSpace(ref) == "" {
251: 		return "", false, fmt.Errorf("git publish: resolve branch ref: %w", err)
252: 	}
253: 	if _, err := gitOutput(ctx, repo, nil, "update-ref", strings.TrimSpace(ref), commit, parent); err != nil {
254: 		return "", false, fmt.Errorf("git publish: branch changed while committing: %w", err)
255: 	}
256: 	resetArgs := append([]string{"reset", "-q", "HEAD", "--"}, paths...)
257: 	if _, err := gitOutput(ctx, repo, nil, resetArgs...); err != nil {
258: 		return commit, true, fmt.Errorf("git publish: reconcile index after commit: %w", err)
259: 	}
260: 	return commit, true, nil
261: }
262: 
263: func gitOutput(ctx context.Context, dir string, extraEnv []string, args ...string) (string, error) {
264: 	return gitInput(ctx, dir, extraEnv, "", args...)
265: }
266: 
267: func gitInput(ctx context.Context, dir string, extraEnv []string, input string, args ...string) (string, error) {
268: 	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", append([]string{"-C", dir}, args...)...)
269: 	cmd.Env = gitEnvironment(extraEnv)
270: 	if input != "" {
271: 		cmd.Stdin = strings.NewReader(input)
272: 	}
273: 	output, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
274: 	if err != nil {
275: 		detail := strings.TrimSpace(string(output))
276: 		if detail == "" {
277: 			detail = err.Error()
278: 		}
279: 		return "", fmt.Errorf("git %s: %s", strings.Join(args, " "), detail)
280: 	}
281: 	return strings.TrimSpace(string(output)), nil
282: }
283: 
284: func gitEnvironment(extra []string) []string {
285: 	overrides := map[string]string{"GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT": "0", "LC_ALL": "C"}
286: 	for _, item := range extra {
287: 		if key, value, ok := strings.Cut(item, "="); ok {
288: 			overrides[key] = value
289: 		}
290: 	}
291: 	env := make([]string, 0, len(os.Environ())+len(overrides))
292: 	for _, item := range os.Environ() {
293: 		key, _, _ := strings.Cut(item, "=")
294: 		if _, replaced := overrides[key]; !replaced {
295: 			env = append(env, item)
296: 		}
297: 	}
298: 	for key, value := range overrides {
299: 		env = append(env, key+"="+value)
300: 	}
301: 	return env
302: }
303: 
304: func validRemoteName(name string) bool {
305: 	if name == "" || strings.HasPrefix(name, "-") {
306: 		return false
307: 	}
308: 	for _, r := range name {
309: 		if (r >= 'a' && r <= 'z') || (r >= 'A' && r <= 'Z') || (r >= '0' && r <= '9') || strings.ContainsRune("._/-", r) {
310: 			continue
311: 		}
312: 		return false
313: 	}
314: 	return true
315: }

(End of file - total 315 lines)
</content>

242: 		if se.Category == "review_gate" || se.Category == "catalog" {
243: 			return AttemptBlocked
244: 		}
245: 	}
246: 	if status == SmokeCompleted {
247: 		return AttemptCompleted
248: 	}
249: 	return AttemptFailed
250: }

293: 	} else if state.Smoke == nil {

295: 	} else if data != nil {

297: 		if state.Smoke.SmokeFingerprint != fingerprint {

299: 		}
300: 	}
301: 	return ValidationResult{Project: sp.Project, Sprint: sp.Slug, Artifact: ArtifactRelPath(sp, StageSmoke), Findings: findings}, nil
302: }

304: func validateSmokeRun(p smokePrepared, discovery smokeDiscovery, selection smokeSelection, response smokeRunResponse, proc pprocess.Result) ([]SmokeEvidence, []SmokeIssue, []SmokeTestResult, error) {
305: 	if response.SchemaVersion != 1 || response.ProtocolVersion != p.Manifest.ProtocolVersion || response.HarnessID != p.Manifest.Harness.ID || response.RunID == "" {
306: 		return nil, nil, nil, smokeError("smoke_evidence_identity", "evidence", "run identity does not match manifest/discovery", "Inspect the external run response.", nil)
307: 	}
308: 	if response.ScopeKind != selection.Kind || strings.Join(response.Scope, ",") != strings.Join(selection.IDs, ",") {
309: 		return nil, nil, nil, smokeError("smoke_evidence_scope", "evidence", "reported scope does not match the request", "Fix the harness scope identity.", nil)
310: 	}
311: 	c := response.Counts
312: 	if c.Total < 0 || c.Passed < 0 || c.Failed < 0 || c.Skipped < 0 || c.Errors < 0 || c.Passed+c.Failed+c.Skipped+c.Errors != c.Total {
313: 		return nil, nil, nil, smokeError("smoke_evidence_counts", "evidence", "result counts are inconsistent", "Fix the harness count summary.", nil)
314: 	}
315: 	if response.DurationMs < 0 || len(response.Evidence) == 0 {
316: 		return nil, nil, nil, smokeError("smoke_evidence_missing", "evidence", "duration or evidence identity is missing", "Emit complete protocol-v1 evidence.", nil)
317: 	}
318: 	expected := expectedSmokeTests(discovery, selection)
319: 	actual := make([]string, 0, len(response.Tests))
320: 	statusCounts := SmokeCountsWire{}
321: 	for _, test := range response.Tests {
322: 		if test.ID == "" {
323: 			return nil, nil, nil, smokeError("smoke_evidence_tests", "evidence", "run contains an empty test identity", "Return every executed discovered test identity.", nil)
324: 		}
325: 		actual = append(actual, test.ID)
326: 		switch test.Status {
327: 		case "passed":
328: 			statusCounts.Passed++
329: 		case "failed":
330: 			statusCounts.Failed++
331: 		case "skipped":
332: 			statusCounts.Skipped++
333: 		case "error":
334: 			statusCounts.Errors++
335: 		default:
336: 			return nil, nil, nil, smokeError("smoke_evidence_tests", "evidence", "run contains an unsupported test status", "Use passed, failed, skipped, or error.", nil)
337: 		}
338: 	}
339: 	statusCounts.Total = len(response.Tests)
340: 	sort.Strings(expected)
341: 	sort.Strings(actual)
342: 	if strings.Join(expected, "\x00") != strings.Join(actual, "\x00") || statusCounts != c {
343: 		return nil, nil, nil, smokeError("smoke_evidence_tests", "evidence", "executed test identities/statuses do not match discovery and counts", "Run exactly the selected discovered tests and return their identities.", nil)
344: 	}
345: 	var evidence []SmokeEvidence
346: 	for _, item := range response.Evidence {
347: 		root := p.RunsRoot
348: 		if item.Kind == "issue" {
349: 			root = p.IssuesRoot
350: 		}
351: 		full := item.Path
352: 		if !filepath.IsAbs(full) {
353: 			full = filepath.Join(p.HarnessRoot, filepath.FromSlash(full))
354: 		}
355: 		resolved, err := canonicalFileInside(root, full)
356: 		if err != nil {
357: 			return nil, nil, nil, smokeError("smoke_evidence_path", "evidence", "evidence path escapes or is missing", "Keep evidence inside declared roots.", err)
358: 		}
359: 		info, err := os.Stat(resolved)
360: 		if err != nil {
361: 			return nil, nil, nil, err
362: 		}
363: 		hash, err := hashFile(resolved)
364: 		if err != nil {
365: 			return nil, nil, nil, err
366: 		}
367: 		if item.SHA256 != "" && !strings.EqualFold(item.SHA256, hash) {
368: 			return nil, nil, nil, smokeError("smoke_evidence_hash", "evidence", "evidence hash mismatch", "Restore immutable run evidence or rerun smoke.", nil)
369: 		}
370: 		if !strings.Contains(filepath.Base(resolved), response.RunID) && item.Kind != "issue" {
371: 			return nil, nil, nil, smokeError("smoke_evidence_run", "evidence", "evidence path does not identify the reported run", "Use run-ID-addressed evidence.", nil)
372: 		}
373: 		evidence = append(evidence, SmokeEvidence{Kind: item.Kind, Path: resolved, SHA256: hash, Size: info.Size(), ModifiedAt: info.ModTime().UTC()})
374: 	}
375: 	issues := append([]SmokeIssue(nil), response.Issues...)
376: 	failedTests := make(map[string]struct{}, c.Failed+c.Errors)
377: 	for _, test := range response.Tests {
378: 		if test.Status == "failed" || test.Status == "error" {
379: 			failedTests[test.ID] = struct{}{}
380: 		}
381: 	}
382: 	filedTests := make(map[string]struct{}, len(issues))
383: 	for i := range issues {
384: 		if issues[i].ID == "" || (issues[i].Status != "open" && issues[i].Status != "resolved") {
385: 			return nil, nil, nil, smokeError("smoke_issue_identity", "evidence", "issue identity/status is invalid", "Emit open or resolved issue metadata.", nil)
386: 		}
387: 		full := issues[i].Path
388: 		if !filepath.IsAbs(full) {
389: 			full = filepath.Join(p.HarnessRoot, filepath.FromSlash(full))
390: 		}
391: 		resolved, err := canonicalFileInside(p.IssuesRoot, full)
392: 		if err != nil || !strings.Contains(filepath.Base(resolved), issues[i].ID) {
393: 			return nil, nil, nil, smokeError("smoke_issue_path", "evidence", "issue path is missing, escaping, or mismatched", "Use an issue-ID-addressed file under the issues root.", err)
394: 		}
395: 		issues[i].Path = resolved
396: 		if _, failed := failedTests[issues[i].TestID]; failed && issues[i].Status == "open" {
397: 			filedTests[issues[i].TestID] = struct{}{}
398: 		}
399: 		if issues[i].Status == "open" && (issues[i].TestID == "" || issues[i].Severity == "" || issues[i].Title == "" || issues[i].Summary == "" || issues[i].Theory == "" || issues[i].Evidence == "" || issues[i].Action == "") {
400: 			return nil, nil, nil, smokeError("smoke_issue_detail", "evidence", "open issue metadata is incomplete", "For every open issue emit test_id, severity, title, summary, theory, evidence, and action.", nil)
401: 		}
402: 	}
403: 	for testID := range failedTests {
404: 		if _, ok := filedTests[testID]; !ok {
405: 			return nil, nil, nil, smokeError("smoke_issue_missing", "evidence", "failed test has no detailed open issue: "+testID, "File and return one detailed issue for every failed or errored test.", nil)
406: 		}
407: 	}
408: 	if proc.ExitCode != 0 && c.Failed+c.Errors == 0 {
409: 		return nil, nil, nil, smokeError("smoke_process_unexplained", "process", "non-zero process exit has no matching failed evidence", "Inspect external evidence before retrying.", nil)
410: 	}
411: 	return evidence, issues, append([]SmokeTestResult(nil), response.Tests...), nil
412: }

414: func expectedSmokeTests(discovery smokeDiscovery, selection smokeSelection) []string {
415: 	testBySuite := map[string][]string{}

432: 				}
433: 			}
434: 		}
435: 	}
436: 	return out
437: }

439: func (s Service) commitSmoke(p smokePrepared, result SmokeResult) (SmokeResult, error) {
440: 	content := RenderSmoke(result)
441: 	if findings := ValidateSmokeContent(content); len(findings) > 0 {
442: 		return smokeFailedResult(result, smokeError("smoke_artifact_validation", "validation", findings[0].Problem, findings[0].Suggestion, nil))
443: 	}
444: 	path, err := ArtifactPath(s.root, p.Sprint, StageSmoke)
445: 	if err != nil {
446: 		return smokeFailedResult(result, err)
447: 	}
448: 	if err := atomicWriteFile(path, []byte(content)); err != nil {
449: 		return smokeFailedResult(result, smokeError("smoke_persistence", "persistence", "smoke summary could not be committed", "The previous valid summary was preserved.", err))
450: 	}
451: 	state, err := LoadFlowState(s.root, p.Sprint)
452: 	if err != nil {
453: 		result.Reconciliation = true
454: 		return result, smokeError("smoke_reconciliation", "reconciliation", "smoke.md committed but flow state could not be loaded", "Reconcile flow state by rerunning smoke.", err)
455: 	}
456: 	now := s.now().UTC()
457: 	evidenceID := ""
458: 	if len(result.Evidence) > 0 {
459: 		evidenceID = result.Evidence[0].SHA256
460: 	}
461: 	artifactDigest := hashBytes([]byte(content))
462: 	identityRefs := smokeIdentityReferences(p, result)
463: 	inputFingerprint, _ := refreshEvidenceFingerprint(identityRefs)
464: 	refs := make([]EvidenceReference, 0, len(result.Evidence))
465: 	for _, evidence := range result.Evidence {
466: 		refs = append(refs, EvidenceReference{Kind: evidence.Kind, Path: evidence.Path, Digest: evidence.SHA256})
467: 	}
468: 	var override *DiagnosticOverride
469: 	if result.ReviewOverride {
470: 		override = &DiagnosticOverride{Requested: true, Confirmed: true, Rationale: result.OverrideRationale, RequestedAt: now, ReviewFingerprint: result.ReviewFingerprint, ReviewVerdict: string(result.ReviewVerdict)}
471: 	}
472: 	active := (*VerificationAttempt)(nil)
473: 	if state.Smoke != nil {
474: 		active = state.Smoke.ActiveAttempt
475: 	}
476: 	state.Smoke = &SmokeStageState{Status: result.Status, Verdict: result.Verdict, Path: ArtifactRelPath(p.Sprint, StageSmoke), LastRunAt: &now, ReviewFingerprint: result.ReviewFingerprint, SmokeFingerprint: artifactDigest, ArtifactDigest: artifactDigest, InputFingerprint: inputFingerprint, RunID: result.RunID, AuthorRunID: result.AuthorRunID, AuthorModel: result.AuthorModel, AuthorChangedPaths: append([]string(nil), result.AuthorChangedPaths...), CoverageMapping: result.CoverageMapping, EvidenceID: evidenceID, ReviewOverride: result.ReviewOverride, Diagnostics: result.Diagnostics, Issues: append([]SmokeIssue(nil), result.Issues...), Evidence: refs, Override: override, ActiveAttempt: active, LastComplete: &SmokeCompletion{Verdict: result.Verdict, Artifact: ArtifactRelPath(p.Sprint, StageSmoke), ArtifactDigest: artifactDigest, InputFingerprint: inputFingerprint, CompletedAt: now, RunID: result.RunID, AuthorRunID: result.AuthorRunID, AuthorModel: result.AuthorModel, AuthorChangedPaths: append([]string(nil), result.AuthorChangedPaths...), CoverageMapping: result.CoverageMapping, EvidenceID: evidenceID, Evidence: identityRefs, Issues: append([]SmokeIssue(nil), result.Issues...), Override: override}}
477: 	if err := SaveFlowState(s.root, p.Sprint, state); err != nil {
478: 		result.Reconciliation = true
479: 		return result, smokeError("smoke_reconciliation", "reconciliation", "smoke.md committed but flow state update failed", "Reconcile flow state by rerunning smoke.", err)
480: 	}
481: 	return result, nil
482: }

514: 	if len(r.Tests) > 0 {

539: 		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- Working theory: %s\n", printable(issue.Theory))
540: 		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- Supporting evidence: %s\n", printable(issue.Evidence))
541: 		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- Next investigation: %s\n\n", printable(issue.Action))
542: 	}
543: 	if len(r.Diagnostics) == 0 && findings == 0 {
544: 		b.WriteString("- none\n")
545: 	} else {
546: 		for _, diagnostic := range r.Diagnostics {
547: 			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- %s\n", printable(diagnostic))
548: 		}
549: 	}
550: 	b.WriteString("\n## Open Issues\n\n")
551: 	open := false
552: 	for _, issue := range r.Issues {
553: 		if issue.Status == "open" {
554: 			open = true
555: 			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- `%s` (%s, test `%s`): `%s`\n", issue.ID, printable(issue.Severity), printable(issue.TestID), issue.Path)
556: 		}
557: 	}
558: 	if !open {
559: 		b.WriteString("- none\n")
560: 	}
561: 	b.WriteString("\n## Resolved Issues\n\n")
562: 	resolved := false
563: 	for _, issue := range r.Issues {
564: 		if issue.Status == "resolved" {
565: 			resolved = true
566: 			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- `%s` `%s`\n", issue.ID, issue.Path)
567: 		}
568: 	}
569: 	if !resolved {
570: 		b.WriteString("- none\n")
571: 	}
572: 	b.WriteString("\n## Mutation And Safety Check\n\nOnly smoke.md, flow-state.json, manifest-declared harness authoring paths, and manifest-declared external evidence roots were approved for mutation. Product source and governed sprint inputs were identity-checked before and after authoring.\n\n")
573: 	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "## Verdict And Next Action\n\nVerdict: `%s`\nNext action: %s\n", r.Verdict, printable(r.NextAction))
574: 	return b.String()
575: }

577: func ValidateSmokeContent(content string) []ValidationFinding {
578: 	var findings []ValidationFinding
579: 	if strings.TrimSpace(content) == "" || containsPlaceholder(content) {
580: 		findings = append(findings, finding("smoke.md", "", "", "empty or placeholder smoke summary", "summary is incomplete", "Generate a complete evidence-backed summary."))
581: 	}
582: 	for _, heading := range []string{"Smoke Context", "Review Gate", "Harness And Protocol", "Smoke Authoring", "Selected Scope And Rationale", "Preconditions And Environment", "Safe Invocation", "Run Evidence", "Findings", "Open Issues", "Resolved Issues", "Mutation And Safety Check", "Verdict And Next Action"} {
583: 		if !markdownHeadingPresent(content, heading) {
584: 			findings = append(findings, finding("smoke.md", heading, "", "missing required section", "section was not found", "Regenerate smoke.md."))
585: 		}
586: 	}
587: 	verdict := SmokeVerdict(fieldBacktick(content, "Verdict:"))
588: 	if !validSmokeVerdict(verdict) {
589: 		findings = append(findings, finding("smoke.md", "Verdict", "", "invalid verdict", string(verdict), "Use one of the five smoke verdicts."))
590: 	}
591: 	for _, forbidden := range []string{"-----BEGIN", "Authorization: Bearer", "\"stdout\":", "\"stderr\":"} {
592: 		if strings.Contains(content, forbidden) {
593: 			findings = append(findings, finding("smoke.md", "Safety", "", "raw or secret-bearing content detected", forbidden, "Keep raw streams and secrets in external evidence only."))
594: 		}
595: 	}
596: 	if !strings.Contains(content, "Next action:") {
597: 		findings = append(findings, finding("smoke.md", "Next Action", "", "next action is missing", "no actionable terminal guidance", "Record the required next action."))
598: 	}
599: 	sortSprintFindings(findings)
600: 	return findings
601: }

603: func classifyProcessSmokeError(stage string, result pprocess.Result, err error) error {
604: 	switch {
605: 	case result.TimedOut:
606: 		return smokeError("smoke_timeout", "timeout", stage+" timed out", "Inspect external evidence and retry with a bounded timeout.", err)
607: 	case result.Cancelled || errors.Is(err, context.Canceled):
608: 		return smokeError("smoke_cancelled", "cancellation", stage+" was cancelled", "Confirm cleanup before retrying.", err)
609: 	case !result.CleanupComplete:
610: 		return smokeError("smoke_cleanup", "cleanup", stage+" cleanup is uncertain", "Terminate owned descendants before retrying.", err)
611: 	default:

312: 	if c.Total < 0 || c.Passed < 0 || c.Failed < 0 || c.Skipped < 0 || c.Errors < 0 || c.Passed+c.Failed+c.Skipped+c.Errors != c.Total {
313: 		return nil, nil, nil, smokeError("smoke_evidence_counts", "evidence", "result counts are inconsistent", "Fix the harness count summary.", nil)
314: 	}
315: 	if response.DurationMs < 0 || len(response.Evidence) == 0 {
316: 		return nil, nil, nil, smokeError("smoke_evidence_missing", "evidence", "duration or evidence identity is missing", "Emit complete protocol-v1 evidence.", nil)
317: 	}
318: 	expected := expectedSmokeTests(discovery, selection)
319: 	actual := make([]string, 0, len(response.Tests))
320: 	statusCounts := SmokeCountsWire{}
321: 	for _, test := range response.Tests {
322: 		if test.ID == "" {
323: 			return nil, nil, nil, smokeError("smoke_evidence_tests", "evidence", "run contains an empty test identity", "Return every executed discovered test identity.", nil)
324: 		}
325: 		actual = append(actual, test.ID)
326: 		switch test.Status {
327: 		case "passed":
328: 			statusCounts.Passed++
329: 		case "failed":
330: 			statusCounts.Failed++
331: 		case "skipped":
332: 			statusCounts.Skipped++
333: 		case "error":
334: 			statusCounts.Errors++
335: 		default:
336: 			return nil, nil, nil, smokeError("smoke_evidence_tests", "evidence", "run contains an unsupported test status", "Use passed, failed, skipped, or error.", nil)
337: 		}
338: 	}
339: 	statusCounts.Total = len(response.Tests)
340: 	sort.Strings(expected)
341: 	sort.Strings(actual)
342: 	if strings.Join(expected, "\x00") != strings.Join(actual, "\x00") || statusCounts != c {
343: 		return nil, nil, nil, smokeError("smoke_evidence_tests", "evidence", "executed test identities/statuses do not match discovery and counts", "Run exactly the selected discovered tests and return their identities.", nil)
344: 	}
345: 	var evidence []SmokeEvidence
346: 	for _, item := range response.Evidence {
347: 		root := p.RunsRoot
348: 		if item.Kind == "issue" {
349: 			root = p.IssuesRoot
350: 		}
351: 		full := item.Path
352: 		if !filepath.IsAbs(full) {
353: 			full = filepath.Join(p.HarnessRoot, filepath.FromSlash(full))
354: 		}
355: 		resolved, err := canonicalFileInside(root, full)
356: 		if err != nil {
357: 			return nil, nil, nil, smokeError("smoke_evidence_path", "evidence", "evidence path escapes or is missing", "Keep evidence inside declared roots.", err)
358: 		}
359: 		info, err := os.Stat(resolved)
360: 		if err != nil {
361: 			return nil, nil, nil, err
362: 		}
363: 		hash, err := hashFile(resolved)
364: 		if err != nil {
365: 			return nil, nil, nil, err
366: 		}
367: 		if item.SHA256 != "" && !strings.EqualFold(item.SHA256, hash) {
368: 			return nil, nil, nil, smokeError("smoke_evidence_hash", "evidence", "evidence hash mismatch", "Restore immutable run evidence or rerun smoke.", nil)
369: 		}
370: 		if !strings.Contains(filepath.Base(resolved), response.RunID) && item.Kind != "issue" {
371: 			return nil, nil, nil, smokeError("smoke_evidence_run", "evidence", "evidence path does not identify the reported run", "Use run-ID-addressed evidence.", nil)
372: 		}
373: 		evidence = append(evidence, SmokeEvidence{Kind: item.Kind, Path: resolved, SHA256: hash, Size: info.Size(), ModifiedAt: info.ModTime().UTC()})
374: 	}
375: 	issues := append([]SmokeIssue(nil), response.Issues...)
376: 	failedTests := make(map[string]struct{}, c.Failed+c.Errors)
377: 	for _, test := range response.Tests {
378: 		if test.Status == "failed" || test.Status == "error" {
379: 			failedTests[test.ID] = struct{}{}
380: 		}
381: 	}
382: 	filedTests := make(map[string]struct{}, len(issues))
383: 	for i := range issues {
384: 		if issues[i].ID == "" || (issues[i].Status != "open" && issues[i].Status != "resolved") {
385: 			return nil, nil, nil, smokeError("smoke_issue_identity", "evidence", "issue identity/status is invalid", "Emit open or resolved issue metadata.", nil)
386: 		}
387: 		full := issues[i].Path
388: 		if !filepath.IsAbs(full) {
389: 			full = filepath.Join(p.HarnessRoot, filepath.FromSlash(full))
390: 		}
391: 		resolved, err := canonicalFileInside(p.IssuesRoot, full)
392: 		if err != nil || !strings.Contains(filepath.Base(resolved), issues[i].ID) {
393: 			return nil, nil, nil, smokeError("smoke_issue_path", "evidence", "issue path is missing, escaping, or mismatched", "Use an issue-ID-addressed file under the issues root.", err)
394: 		}
395: 		issues[i].Path = resolved
396: 		if _, failed := failedTests[issues[i].TestID]; failed && issues[i].Status == "open" {
397: 			filedTests[issues[i].TestID] = struct{}{}
398: 		}
399: 		if issues[i].Status == "open" && (issues[i].TestID == "" || issues[i].Severity == "" || issues[i].Title == "" || issues[i].Summary == "" || issues[i].Theory == "" || issues[i].Evidence == "" || issues[i].Action == "") {
400: 			return nil, nil, nil, smokeError("smoke_issue_detail", "evidence", "open issue metadata is incomplete", "For every open issue emit test_id, severity, title, summary, theory, evidence, and action.", nil)
401: 		}
402: 	}
403: 	for testID := range failedTests {
404: 		if _, ok := filedTests[testID]; !ok {
405: 			return nil, nil, nil, smokeError("smoke_issue_missing", "evidence", "failed test has no detailed open issue: "+testID, "File and return one detailed issue for every failed or errored test.", nil)
406: 		}
407: 	}
408: 	if proc.ExitCode != 0 && c.Failed+c.Errors == 0 {
409: 		return nil, nil, nil, smokeError("smoke_process_unexplained", "process", "non-zero process exit has no matching failed evidence", "Inspect external evidence before retrying.", nil)
410: 	}
411: 	return evidence, issues, append([]SmokeTestResult(nil), response.Tests...), nil
412: }

477: 	if err := SaveFlowState(s.root, p.Sprint, state); err != nil {
478: 		result.Reconciliation = true
479: 		return result, smokeError("smoke_reconciliation", "reconciliation", "smoke.md committed but flow state update failed", "Reconcile flow state by rerunning smoke.", err)

482: }

499: 	if mapping := r.CoverageMapping; mapping != nil {

514: 	if len(r.Tests) > 0 {

519: 		b.WriteString("\n")

521: 	b.WriteString("### External Evidence Identity And Links\n\n")
522: 	if len(r.Evidence) == 0 {

524: 	} else {

527: 		}
528: 	}
529: 	b.WriteString("\n## Findings\n\n")
530: 	findings := 0
531: 	for _, issue := range r.Issues {

534: 		}

539: 		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- Working theory: %s\n", printable(issue.Theory))
540: 		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- Supporting evidence: %s\n", printable(issue.Evidence))
541: 		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- Next investigation: %s\n\n", printable(issue.Action))
542: 	}
543: 	if len(r.Diagnostics) == 0 && findings == 0 {
544: 		b.WriteString("- none\n")
545: 	} else {
546: 		for _, diagnostic := range r.Diagnostics {
547: 			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- %s\n", printable(diagnostic))
548: 		}
549: 	}
550: 	b.WriteString("\n## Open Issues\n\n")
551: 	open := false
552: 	for _, issue := range r.Issues {
553: 		if issue.Status == "open" {
554: 			open = true
555: 			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- `%s` (%s, test `%s`): `%s`\n", issue.ID, printable(issue.Severity), printable(issue.TestID), issue.Path)
556: 		}
557: 	}
558: 	if !open {
559: 		b.WriteString("- none\n")
560: 	}
561: 	b.WriteString("\n## Resolved Issues\n\n")
562: 	resolved := false
563: 	for _, issue := range r.Issues {
564: 		if issue.Status == "resolved" {
565: 			resolved = true
566: 			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- `%s` `%s`\n", issue.ID, issue.Path)
567: 		}
568: 	}
569: 	if !resolved {
570: 		b.WriteString("- none\n")
571: 	}
572: 	b.WriteString("\n## Mutation And Safety Check\n\nOnly smoke.md, flow-state.json, manifest-declared harness authoring paths, and manifest-declared external evidence roots were approved for mutation. Product source and governed sprint inputs were identity-checked before and after authoring.\n\n")
573: 	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "## Verdict And Next Action\n\nVerdict: `%s`\nNext action: %s\n", r.Verdict, printable(r.NextAction))
574: 	return b.String()
575: }

577: func ValidateSmokeContent(content string) []ValidationFinding {
578: 	var findings []ValidationFinding
579: 	if strings.TrimSpace(content) == "" || containsPlaceholder(content) {
580: 		findings = append(findings, finding("smoke.md", "", "", "empty or placeholder smoke summary", "summary is incomplete", "Generate a complete evidence-backed summary."))
581: 	}
582: 	for _, heading := range []string{"Smoke Context", "Review Gate", "Harness And Protocol", "Smoke Authoring", "Selected Scope And Rationale", "Preconditions And Environment", "Safe Invocation", "Run Evidence", "Findings", "Open Issues", "Resolved Issues", "Mutation And Safety Check", "Verdict And Next Action"} {
583: 		if !markdownHeadingPresent(content, heading) {
584: 			findings = append(findings, finding("smoke.md", heading, "", "missing required section", "section was not found", "Regenerate smoke.md."))
585: 		}
586: 	}
587: 	verdict := SmokeVerdict(fieldBacktick(content, "Verdict:"))
588: 	if !validSmokeVerdict(verdict) {
589: 		findings = append(findings, finding("smoke.md", "Verdict", "", "invalid verdict", string(verdict), "Use one of the five smoke verdicts."))
590: 	}
591: 	for _, forbidden := range []string{"-----BEGIN", "Authorization: Bearer", "\"stdout\":", "\"stderr\":"} {
592: 		if strings.Contains(content, forbidden) {
593: 			findings = append(findings, finding("smoke.md", "Safety", "", "raw or secret-bearing content detected", forbidden, "Keep raw streams and secrets in external evidence only."))
594: 		}
595: 	}
596: 	if !strings.Contains(content, "Next action:") {
597: 		findings = append(findings, finding("smoke.md", "Next Action", "", "next action is missing", "no actionable terminal guidance", "Record the required next action."))
598: 	}
599: 	sortSprintFindings(findings)
600: 	return findings
601: }

603: func classifyProcessSmokeError(stage string, result pprocess.Result, err error) error {
604: 	switch {
605: 	case result.TimedOut:
606: 		return smokeError("smoke_timeout", "timeout", stage+" timed out", "Inspect external evidence and retry with a bounded timeout.", err)
607: 	case result.Cancelled || errors.Is(err, context.Canceled):
608: 		return smokeError("smoke_cancelled", "cancellation", stage+" was cancelled", "Confirm cleanup before retrying.", err)
609: 	case !result.CleanupComplete:
610: 		return smokeError("smoke_cleanup", "cleanup", stage+" cleanup is uncertain", "Terminate owned descendants before retrying.", err)
611: 	default:
612: 		return smokeError("smoke_process", "process", stage+" process failed", "Inspect the safe diagnostic and external harness logs.", err)
613: 	}
614: }

625: func decodeOneJSON(value string, target any) error {
626: 	dec := json.NewDecoder(strings.NewReader(strings.TrimSpace(value)))
627: 	if err := dec.Decode(target); err != nil {
628: 		return err
629: 	}
630: 	var extra any
631: 	if err := dec.Decode(&extra); err == nil {
632: 		return fmt.Errorf("multiple JSON values")
633: 	} else if !errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
634: 		return err
635: 	}
636: 	return nil
637: }
638: func safeArgv(executable string, args []string) string {
639: 	// Manifest argv has no sensitivity metadata, so stable output retains only
640: 	// option names and argument shape. Raw values remain in external evidence.
641: 	values := []string{filepath.Base(executable)}
642: 	for _, value := range args {
643: 		if strings.HasPrefix(value, "-") {
644: 			if name, _, ok := strings.Cut(value, "="); ok {
645: 				values = append(values, name+"=[REDACTED]")
646: 			} else {
647: 				values = append(values, value)
648: 			}
649: 			continue
650: 		}
651: 		values = append(values, "[ARG]")
652: 	}
653: 	for i, value := range values {
654: 		values[i] = fmt.Sprintf("%q", value)
655: 	}
656: 	return strings.Join(values, " ")
657: }

666: func synthesizeSmokeVerdict(counts SmokeCounts, issues []SmokeIssue) SmokeVerdict {
667: 	if counts.Failed > 0 || counts.Errors > 0 {
668: 		return SmokeFailVerdict
669: 	}
670: 	if hasOpenSmokeIssues(issues) {
671: 		return SmokePassWithOpenIssues
672: 	}
673: 	return SmokePass

675: func nextSmokeAction(r SmokeResult) string {
676: 	switch r.Verdict {
677: 	case SmokePass:
678: 		return "Deep smoke is complete; proceed to the next roadmap stage."
679: 	case SmokePassWithOpenIssues:
680: 		return "Review the linked open issues before proceeding."
681: 	case SmokeFailVerdict:
682: 		return "Inspect linked evidence, fix the selected-smoke failures, and rerun the containing suite."
683: 	case SmokeBlockedVerdict:
684: 		return "Satisfy the blocked prerequisite or coverage requirement and rerun smoke."
685: 	case SmokeNotApplicable:
686: 		return "No smoke action is required for this sprint."
687: 	}
688: 	return "Inspect smoke diagnostics."
689: }
690: func fieldBacktick(content, prefix string) string {
691: 	for _, line := range strings.Split(content, "\n") {
692: 		if strings.HasPrefix(strings.TrimSpace(line), prefix) {
693: 			return strings.Trim(strings.TrimSpace(strings.TrimPrefix(strings.TrimSpace(line), prefix)), "`")
694: 		}
695: 	}
696: 	return ""
697: }
698: func printable(value string) string {
699: 	value = strings.TrimSpace(value)
700: 	if value == "" {
701: 		return "none"
702: 	}
703: 	value = strings.ReplaceAll(value, "`", "'")
704: 	return value
705: }
706: func hashBytes(data []byte) string { sum := sha256.Sum256(data); return hex.EncodeToString(sum[:]) }
707: func hashFile(path string) (string, error) {
708: 	data, err := os.ReadFile(path)
709: 	if err != nil {
710: 		return "", err
711: 	}
712: 	return hashBytes(data), nil

Interesting. In `RunSmoke` (smoke.go:39-59):

1. Line 39-48: If smoke passed, marks roadmap.md as delivered (writes to filesystem).
2. Line 49-59: If completed, publishes (commits) smoke.md, flow-state.json, and — if pass & non-diagnostic — roadmap.md.

Ordering: durable state commit happens in `runSmoke` → `commitSmoke` before publication. Roadmap mark happens after `commitSmoke`, before publish. Publication includes roadmap.md. That ordering is fine: mark-then-publish means the published content includes the mark. But note: if `MarkRoadmapSprintDelivered` fails at line 45, returns early with error — no publication of smoke.md/flow-state even though they're durably committed. That's consistent with "publication always ordered after durable state" — failure just means un-published; retry would re-publish. OK.

Wait, there's a subtle issue at line 44: `roadmapPath := filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(filepath.Dir(sp.Path)), "roadmap.md")`. In publication.go line 116 the same computation: `filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(filepath.Dir(prepared.Sprint.Path)), "roadmap.md")`.

What is `sp.Path`? Need to check sprint path structure. Let me find how Sprint.Path is constructed. Probably `<root>/projects/<project>/sprints/<slug>`? Then Dir(Dir(sp.Path)) = `<root>/projects/<project>` → roadmap.md there? Or is it `<root>/<project>/sprints/<slug>`, giving `<root>/<project>/roadmap.md`. Need to verify against project layout and MarkRoadmapSprintDelivered usage elsewhere.

Also interesting: in `RunSmoke`, when verdict == SmokePassWithOpenIssues, roadmap not marked (line 39 requires SmokePass). But publication.go line 115 also requires SmokePass && !DiagnosticOnly for including roadmap.md. Consistent.

But hold on — there's a mismatch possibility: RunSmoke marks roadmap when `result.Verdict == SmokePass && !result.DiagnosticOnly && (result.ReviewVerdict == ReviewPass || ReviewPassWithFindings)` — includes review-verdict condition. publication.go's workspacePaths condition doesn't check ReviewVerdict. But if review verdict isn't pass, roadmap wasn't marked on disk, so publishing roadmap.md would be a no-op tree-equal → committed=false. Not a bug per se... unless roadmap.md has other uncommitted changes from user! Hmm — publishing a path set includes whatever working-tree changes exist for those paths. If the user had unrelated uncommitted modifications to roadmap.md, ultraplan would commit them. That's inherent to path-set-based publication though ("owned paths" = roadmap.md is owned). Fine.

Now the deeper question about `publishSmokeStage`: `prepared.Sprint.Path` vs `sp.Path` should be same.

On retry of execute... `allExecuteTasksResolved` still true → republish. Implementation publish again: commitPaths — tree equals parent tree now (already committed) → no new commit; then pushes again. So retry converges. OK.

For smoke harness publish: `Root: prepared.HarnessRoot`, paths joined with HarnessRoot. Fine.

### Candidate 3: **`commitPaths` index reconciliation uses `git reset -q HEAD -- paths`** — wait, there's a subtlety. After `update-ref` moves the branch to the new commit, the *user's real index* still reflects the old HEAD plus user's staged changes. For owned paths that were previously committed by ultraplan, resetting them to new HEAD is right.

BUT: consider a path that the user had *staged* modifications for, which is also an owned path. The temp-index commit commits the working-tree state (`git add -A` takes working tree content), discarding the distinction between staged vs unstaged for owned paths. Then reset makes index match HEAD for those paths — user's staged state for owned paths is overwritten. That's inherent to "owned paths" design — acceptable, documented? Probably fine.

More interesting: what about **unstaged deletion of an owned path**? `git add -A -- <path>` stages the deletion, commits it. Working tree matches. Fine.

What about **ignored files** among owned paths? `git add -A` respects .gitignore unless -f. So an ignored owned path isn't committed. Fine.

Between `rev-parse HEAD` and `update-ref ref commit parent`, if the branch moved (e.g., user committed concurrently), update-ref fails → error returned. Good — no lost update. But NOTE: `update-ref <ref> <commit> <oldvalue>` verifies current value equals parent. Correct CAS usage.

However — there's a subtle bug candidate: after successful update-ref, they run `git reset -q HEAD -- paths`. If between update-ref and reset another process commits, reset just syncs index entries for owned paths to HEAD — could clobber concurrent committer's staged changes for owned paths. But the flock serializes ultraplan publishers only. External git processes aren't blocked by flock. This race exists but is inherent; severity low, and the lock file is advisory against other ultraplan instances. Hmm, actually two concurrent ultraplane processes on same machine serialize via flock. reasoning_details.text:
OK so DeferPublication is only set in run_loop; direct RunAnalysis/Synthesize callers publish inline. No double publish.

Now let me focus on the verification/operability lens. Key candidates to investigate deeper:

**A. `Publish` push path — `--porcelain` output discarded; but more importantly, is there any logging at all of publication activity?** Let me check how the CLI surfaces publications (FlowResult.Publications rendering). Also check whether errors get logged.

**B. The temp index + `git add -A -- paths` with paths that are OUTSIDE the repo?** Already validated by publishPaths. But wait — for the smoke harness publish: paths are joined from `result.AuthorChangedPaths` rel paths against HarnessRoot. AuthorChangedPaths come from... where? They're validated somewhere (manifest-declared). If a rel path escapes, publishPaths catches it. OK.

**C. `commitPaths` — `git add -A --` with absolute-ish rel paths**: they convert to slash-relative rel paths. Good.

**D. Race between `rev-parse HEAD` (parent) and lock acquisition order**: parent resolved AFTER lock acquired (commitPaths called under lock). Yes — commitPaths is called inside the lock. Parent read inside commitPaths. CAS protects anyway.

**E. Push retry semantics when upstream diverged**: non-ff → error; user resolves. Fine.

**F. What happens on push with `--set-upstream` when remote branch exists with different history?** Non-ff error. Fine.

**G. Now a REAL candidate I want to verify: `branch --show-current` vs worktrees and the update-ref symbolic-ref.** In commitPaths:
```go
ref, err := gitOutput(ctx, repo, nil, "symbolic-ref", "-q", "HEAD")
```
This is resolved INSIDE commitPaths after staging — good, fresher than the earlier branch resolution. But note: if HEAD detached between... they check symbolic-ref -q returns empty → error. OK.

BUT here's a subtle one: earlier in Publish, `branch --show-current` was resolved BEFORE the lock. If the user switches branches while ultraplan holds no lock yet... commitPaths re-resolves ref via symbolic-ref under lock. So commit goes to current branch at commit time. But the PUSH then uses... line 140: `refs/heads/"+branch` — the STALE branch name resolved before the lock! And upstream detection uses stale branch too. And the fallback push uses `"HEAD:refs/heads/"+branch`. So if branch changed between initial resolution and push, ultraplan pushes HEAD (new branch's commit!) to refs/heads/<stale-branch>. That would move another branch to an unrelated commit — externally visible! 

How plausible? User switches branches during a stage run (which takes minutes with LLM agents) — quite plausible actually. Stage completion publishes happen after long-running agent stages. A user switching branches mid-stage is realistic. Then publication commits to the CURRENT branch (correct via symbolic-ref under lock), but pushes that commit to the OLD branch ref on the remote — cross-branch contamination on the shared remote. Consequence: remote branch <old> now contains a commit whose changes belong elsewhere; also --set-upstream sets old branch's upstream. This is a genuine TOCTOU defect: branch resolved once outside the lock, used for push targeting inside/after the lock.

Counter-evidence search: Is there anything re-validating branch == current before push? Looking at Publish lines 87-95 (before lock), 112 (lock), 118-131 (commit or HEAD resolve), 132+ (push using `branch`). No re-check. Test coverage: none pinning branch-switch behavior. Severity: medium (external visibility, effectively irreversible push to wrong ref), confidence high on mechanism, medium-high on real-world trigger. Actually wait — how bad is it? Pushing local HEAD (which is now new branch tip including the new commit) to refs/heads/<stale> on the remote. If stale branch exists remotely and this isn't fast-forward, git rejects (non-FF) — mitigating! If fast-forwardable (e.g., stale branch is behind ancestor), push succeeds and pollutes. Or if stale branch doesn't exist remotely, creates it. So consequence requires FF-or-new-remote-branch. Still a real hazard.

Hmm wait, actually let me double check the ordering again: `branch` is resolved at line 87 BEFORE acquiring the lock at 112. Between those two points there's also `publishPaths` and common-dir resolution. But more importantly, the WHOLE stage execution (minutes) happens before Publish is even called. Within Publish itself the window is small (ms). The bigger risk is not within-Publish TOCTOU but rather: commitPaths uses CURRENT symbolic-ref (correct branch B2), while push targets branch B1 captured milliseconds earlier in the same call. Window is small (ms–s). For a race you'd need a branch switch exactly during Publish. Less likely than "user switched branch before Publish" — but in the latter case, both resolutions happen inside Publish, so both see B2. Wait no: line 87 runs at Publish start. If user switched branch BEFORE Publish started, line 87 sees B2 already. So the inconsistency window = duration of Publish between line 87 and push (~ms to seconds given lock contention could block... lock wait can be LONG — unbounded polling loop until ctx done! If another ultraplan process holds the lock, acquireLock polls indefinitely. Branch could switch during that wait easily).

So scenario: two concurrent stage completions on same repo (lock contention), user switches branch during the wait → first finishes, second acquires lock, commitPaths re-resolves ref → commits to B2 correctly; push targets B1 (captured pre-lock). Real but narrow. I'll report as a finding with honest severity (low-medium, medium confidence).

Actually hold on, let me reconsider: does anything else use `branch` post-lock besides push? Line 126 rev-parse HEAD fallback; line 140 upstream for refs/heads/<branch>; 157 fallback push target. Yes.

3. **No test for upstream-push path** (branch with upstream configured pushes to upstream ref, not policy remote). This is significant: the upstream branch of the code path at line 145-154 is NEVER exercised by tests. The retry test uses origin without upstream → falls into else branch (policy remote + set-upstream). So the entire `upstreamRemote != ""` branch — including the `%!w(<nil>)` error path and the `HEAD:<upstreamRef>` push — has zero coverage. Bugs allowed there: e.g., pushing `HEAD:upstreamRef` where upstreamRef like `refs/heads/main` fine... what about when upstream ref is empty but remotename set (broken config)? Error message with nil wrap. Untested code + error-truth wart.

- logging levels other than `debug`, `info`, `warn`, or `error`.
- unsupported health checks or capabilities.
- unsupported permission defaults or unsupported-behavior values.

Run-state files also carry schema versions. Commands such as `study status`, `study validate`, and `study run-loop` reject unsupported run-state schema versions instead of silently migrating them.

## Runtime And Model Mapping

UltraPlan delegates runtime execution through agentwrap and the OpenCode adapter:

- `agentwrap.executable` maps to `opencode.WithExecutable`.
- `agentwrap.extra_args` maps to OpenCode extra args.
- `agentwrap.env` maps to OpenCode environment additions.
- `models.primary` maps to the primary agentwrap provider/model request.
- `models.default` is used when primary cannot be split into provider/model.
- `models.backup` configures an agentwrap fallback target when it differs from primary.
- `execution.default_timeout` maps to the runtime request timeout.
- `execution.default_retries` configures retry policy attempts.
- `agentwrap.required_health` maps to required runtime health checks.
- `agentwrap.required_capabilities` maps to required runtime capabilities.
- `agentwrap.sandbox`, `agentwrap.permission_mode`, `agentwrap.permission_default`, and `agentwrap.permission_unsupported_behavior` map to agentwrap sandbox and permission policy fields.

UltraPlan does not own OpenCode provider credentials or provider billing. Configure those through OpenCode/provider-native mechanisms.

## Git stage publication

`git.stage_completion` controls publication after a study task or sprint stage has produced valid canonical output and persisted its state. `commit` creates a local commit. `commit-and-push` also pushes the current branch, using its upstream when present or `git.remote` when no upstream exists. `off` preserves the working tree without Git mutation.

UltraPlan commits only paths owned by the completed stage. It leaves unrelated staged and unstaged changes alone. Execute is different because its recorded Git worktree belongs to one sprint; UltraPlan commits the complete worktree change set there. Agents remain prohibited from running `git add`, `git commit`, or `git push` themselves.

A push failure does not reopen a completed product stage. The command returns an error and leaves the local commit in place. Rerunning the stage pushes that commit without creating a duplicate. Git commands never prompt for credentials, and `git.push_timeout` bounds each push attempt.

## Smoke Configuration

Smoke configuration is resolved after manifest defaults and before command/TUI overrides. UltraPlan passes only named environment variables; values never appear in config output, JSON, Markdown, or TUI diagnostics. The built-in platform set is limited to `TMPDIR`, `LANG`, and `LC_ALL`; `PATH` and `HOME` are not forwarded by default. Add a manifest-declared name to `smoke.environment` only when the harness genuinely needs it. The real-harness test lane is opt-in with `ULTRAPLAN_REAL_SMOKE=1`; normal tests never launch it.

## Redaction

UltraPlan redacts sensitive-looking values in config, logs, diagnostics, status output, and health output. Do not place provider tokens in `ultraplan.yml`; prefer runtime-native environment or credential stores. Release evidence must not include provider tokens, full sensitive environment dumps, full prompts, full report bodies, or raw unsafe runtime payloads.
## Run-control retention and quota

The following settings participate in the normal default/YAML/environment/CLI
effective-configuration reporting and are safe to expose through redacted
diagnostics:

display.text:
```bash
ultraplan sprint <project> <sprint> status
ultraplan sprint <project> <sprint> validate requirements
ultraplan sprint <project> <sprint> prompt code-context
ultraplan sprint <project> <sprint> validate code-context
ultraplan sprint <project> <sprint> flow --to code-context
ultraplan sprint <project> <sprint> validate sprint-index
ultraplan sprint <project> <sprint> validate execute
ultraplan sprint <project> <sprint> prompt requirements
ultraplan sprint <project> <sprint> prompt plan
ultraplan sprint <project> <sprint> prompt execute
ultraplan sprint <project> <sprint> flow --to plan --dry-run
ultraplan sprint <project> <sprint> flow --to execute --dry-run
ultraplan sprint <project> <sprint> execute --resume
```

Use `prompt <stage>` before runtime-backed flow to inspect the stage input. Use `flow --to <stage> --dry-run` to preview planned stage execution. Non-dry-run flow can generate planning artifacts when runtime prerequisites are available. While it runs, the CLI prints stage transitions and sanitized runtime progress to stderr, leaving the final result on stdout. The TUI shows the same stage and runtime events in the active operation view for sprint flow, execute, and review.

The first non-dry-run code-context stage creates a linked Git worktree for the sprint. UltraPlan branches from the implementation target's current `HEAD` and stores the assignment in `projects/<project>/sprints/<sprint>/.workspace.json`. Commit or stash changes in the source checkout first. Later stages use the sprint worktree, so edits in another checkout or another sprint do not change this sprint's source. Execution may edit the sprint worktree. UltraPlan will not rebase, retarget, remove, or recreate it automatically.

When `git.stage_completion` is `commit` or `commit-and-push`, UltraPlan publishes each valid completed stage before starting the next one. Study reports and sprint planning artifacts commit only their owned paths in the workspace repository. Execute commits the complete dedicated sprint worktree plus its workspace summary and run state. Review and smoke publish valid canonical evidence even when the verdict fails. Dry runs, cancelled stages, and invalid output never publish.

With `commit-and-push`, UltraPlan pushes the current upstream branch. If the branch has no upstream, it pushes to `git.remote` and sets one. A failed push stops the command but leaves the stage complete and the local commit intact. Retry the same command to finish the push without duplicating the commit.

`code-context` reads the configured implementation target under a restricted read-only runtime policy and atomically replaces only the sprint's `code-context.md` after structural validation. The artifact records paths, exact line ranges, optional symbols, and rationale—not copied source. Downstream agent-backed prompts share the exact requirements and code-context bytes plus transient bounded source excerpts, clearly marked untrusted; the context pack never prevents further live repository inspection. A bad path, range, encoding, containment check, changed read, or 256 KiB shared-prefix budget overflow stops before runtime invocation and leaves the last valid artifacts/state intact.

The planning flow continues through controlled execute from validated `plan.md` tasks. One reusable agent session owns the ordered pending-task queue: its first turn receives shared sprint context and the queue, later tasks use compact continuation turns, and UltraPlan checkpoints task status and evidence between turns. Execute writes `.run-state.json` and `execute.md`; automated review then writes the current `review.md`.

Use the integrated transition after execute:

```bash
ultraplan sprint <project> <sprint> verify --to review --dry-run
ultraplan sprint <project> <sprint> verify --to smoke --dry-run
ultraplan sprint <project> <sprint> verify --to smoke --yes
ultraplan sprint <project> <sprint> validate smoke
```

`verify` requires complete execute evidence, obtains or reuses a current review, then applies the smoke gate. Interrupted reviews resume validated coverage and retained OpenCode sessions by default. Use `review --restart` or `verify --restart-review` when you intentionally want fresh sessions; a restart cannot be combined with focused review.

The smoke preview shows the review gate, sufficient scope, prerequisites, duration/cost class where supplied, safe argv, and external evidence roots. `--force-review` additionally requires `--override-reason` and is diagnostic-only after a current failed/blocked review; it cannot override stale or malformed review evidence or improve the overall assessment. Raw harness evidence stays in its `runs/` and `issues/` directories, while the sprint stores only `smoke.md` and flow state.

Compare with the codebase's own standards:
- Progress messages: redacted at render (`RedactValue("sprint.progress", ...)`, smoke/qa progress).
- study init clone failures: dedicated `redactGitOutput` strips `user:token@host` credentials (init_test.go:143-156 proves the threat model is recognized for git output).
- logging package redacts messages.
- health checks redact error strings.
- runtime SDK details redacted.

But gitpublish errors bypass all of this: `git publish: push origin/main: git push --porcelain -- origin HEAD:refs/heads/main: fatal: unable to access 'https://user:ghp_xxx@github.com/org/repo.git/': ...`.

When remote URL contains userinfo (common pattern: `https://x-access-token:<PAT>@github.com/...` for CI or even local use), git's "unable to access" fatal message includes the URL. Git does NOT strip the password from the URL in that message historically (it strips username only in newer versions? Let me think... There was a change: git 2.x shows the URL; credential redaction in messages was improved at some point — commit "t5551: test that GIT_TRACE_CURL redacts"... Actually git DOES redact when printing URLs in some code paths since ~2.32? Hmm. I recall `die("unable to access '%s'", url)` in http.c prints the URL as-is including userinfo. There were fixes to strip userinfo from some warnings ("redirecting to" messages?) Not fully certain across versions.

The stronger, unambiguous part of the finding: **error-truth/redaction inconsistency** — the repo's own doctrine (docs/configuration.md:234: "UltraPlan redacts sensitive-looking values in config, logs, diagnostics, status output, and health output") and its own practice (redactGitOutput for study init) is not applied to gitpublish/gitpublication errors, which reach stderr raw via fail() and also into TUI operation results / web API responses? Confirmed: no pre-flight repo check for HarnessRoot anywhere; publication is the only place repo-ness is required, and it happens after the smoke run completes, verdict recorded, roadmap marked. Finding stands (with the caveat that it only bites when stage_completion != off AND author changed paths exist).

Interesting: smoke_protocol.go:210 `HarnessRoot: root` — where does root come from? Probably harness dir from project-index. If harness registered under the WORKSPACE repo (e.g., `<workspace>/harness/`), it IS inside the workspace repo → publish works, commits harness files to workspace repo — hmm, that would commit harness paths to the workspace repo under the smoke identity — fine ownership-wise? The workspace publish in same RunSmoke call separately publishes smoke.md/flow-state/roadmap as a SECOND commit. Two commits per smoke. OK.

Now let me finalize by re-examining publisher.go once more for anything missed... 

One more scan of subtle issues:

1. Line 96-99: `paths, err := publishPaths(repo, req.Paths, req.All)` — note `repo` here is toplevel of Root. For execute implementation publish All=true → ["."].

2. Line 118: `if len(paths) > 0` commit; else skip.

3. **Line 125-131**: when no commit made (either len(paths)==0 or tree-equal), resolve HEAD — used as result.Commit and pushed. ✓

4. **Line 132**: ModeCommit returns early ✓ no push.

5. **Line 135**: validRemoteName(policy.Remote) checked only in push path ✓ (commit mode doesn't need remote).

6. **Push upstream branch**: `for-each-ref --format=%(upstream:remotename) refs/heads/<branch>` — if branch was just CREATED by update-ref... branch existed already (symbolic-ref). Fine.

7. What if policy.Remote names a remote that DOESN'T exist? push fails " 'origin' does not appear to be a git repository" → error surfaces with config hint. Fail-closed ✓. Could pre-validate via git remote get-url — not done; error truth acceptable.

8. **`gitInput` builds args without shell** ✓ (exec.CommandContext direct argv) — trust boundary statement holds. Remote name validated against `-` prefix & charset → can't inject option-like refspecs via remote name... wait: remote name goes into `push -- --set-upstream -- <remote> HEAD:refs/heads/<branch>` after `--` separator ✓ so even weird names are treated as remote/refspec operands, not options. Branch name from `branch --show-current` could contain leading dash? Git branch names can't start with dash (ref rules) ✓. upstreamRef from for-each-ref is a full ref ✓. Injection posture solid.

9. `strings.ContainsRune("._/-", r)` allows '/' in remote names — fine.

10. **CombinedOutput + TrimSpace on SUCCESS output**: for `for-each-ref`, trailing newline trimmed ✓. Multi-line warnings would corrupt — noted earlier as minor; LC_ALL=C reduces locale noise but warnings still possible (e.g., "warning: templates not found", core.hooksPath issues?). I'll leave as footnote-level; not reporting standalone.

11. **Result.Commit set even when committed=false** — used by retry test ✓.

12. **Missing `--no-verify`?** push hooks: pre-push hook RUNS during push (user's repo hooks). Docs say agents can't run git; ultraplan running push triggers user's pre-push hooks — could be slow/fail. Acceptable/intended? Probably fine (respects user hooks). Skip.

13. **commit-tree respects user.name/email config** — repos without identity configured → commit-tree fails "unable to auto-detect email" → wrapped error. Test repos configure identity. Real workspaces need git identity — undocumented precondition like harness-repo one. Minor; fold into operability finding? Workspace repo presumably has identity (user owns it). Skip.

14. **Time-of-check on `All` flag with paths ignored**: Request{Paths X, All true} → Paths silently ignored. Callers don't do this. Non-issue.

15. study run_loop: consumer goroutine uses `ctx` captured BEFORE loop; if command ctx has no timeout... bounded by PushTimeout per push ✓.

16. **publishRunLoopState called AFTER `<-publicationDone`** ✓ serialized with flock anyway.

Now compile the final findings list with severity/confidence:

**F1 (Medium-Low severity, High confidence): Stale branch name drives push target; commit target re-resolved under lock but push does not.**
- Evidence: publisher.go:87-94 (branch resolved pre-lock), :249-251 (symbolic-ref re-resolved in commitPaths under lock), :140/:149/:154/:157 (push derives refs/heads/<branch> + upstream lookup from stale value).
- Bad outcome: commit lands on current branch B2; push sends B2's HEAD (including unrelated local commits) to refs/heads/<B1> on remote or re-binds B1's upstream (--set-upstream); externally visible cross-branch contamination.
- Trigger: branch switch between line 87 and push — includes unbounded lock-wait window (lock_unix.go:22-39).
- Controls/counter-evidence: CAS protects commit correctness only; no test covers branch switch; non-FF protection limits but doesn't prevent (FF case / new branch creation).
- Regression test: hold ultraplan-publish.lock externally, start Publish goroutine, switch branch while blocked, release, assert pushed ref == branch at push time (or assert failure).

**F2 (Low-Medium severity security/error-truth, High confidence): Publication errors embed raw combined git output; bypass project's own redaction standard.**
- Evidence: publisher.go:273-279 (CombinedOutput → error verbatim); init_clone.go:44-48,52-65 (redactGitOutput applied for clone — precedent); app.go:229-235 fail() prints err raw; sprint flow.go:152/172/218 emit raw into progress (render-side RedactValue keyword-only, redaction.go:28-41 misses `scheme://user:pass@host` without keywords).
- Bad outcome: credential-bearing remote URL (PAT-in-URL setups) printed to stderr/TUI/web operation results on any failed push.
- Trigger: mode=commit-and-push, network/auth failure, remote URL embedding credentials.
- Fix: apply credentialURLPattern-style redaction in gitInput error wrapping (+ bound length like 4096).

**F3 (Medium operability at risk, Medium-High confidence): Smoke harness publication requires harness root to be inside a git repo, validated only post-completion.**
- Evidence: publication.go:100-109 (harness Publish first), publisher.go:79-82 (rev-parse failure = hard error), smoke.go:49-58 (errors.Join after verdict recorded & roadmap marked at :39-48).
- Bad outcome: with stage_completion≠off and authored harness changes, a non-repo harness makes every RunSmoke exit non-zero after fully recording success; permanent retry loop; roadmap marked delivered while command reports failure (mixed state visible to automation).
- Counter-evidence: consistent fail-closed doctrine for publication failures; docs silent on harness repo requirement (planning-smoke.md lists prerequisites without git).
- Fix: pre-flight validation in prepareSmokeStatic (fail before running) OR skip-with-diagnostic for non-repo roots; document requirement.

**F4 (Low severity, High confidence): Verification gaps — entire upstream push path + 3 of 5 adapter publishers + lock concurrency have zero test coverage; misleading test name.**
- Evidence: publisher_test.go tests only fallback-remote push (no upstream configured) — grep confirms no other real-Publish usage; sprint publication_test.go covers only planning+execute; nothing calls publishReviewStage/publishSmokeStage/publishRunLoopState/publishRunAllSummary; lock_unix acquire/release untested; TestPublisherRetriesPushWithoutDuplicateCommit actually asserts idempotent manual rerun, not automatic retry (name misleads).

- Also ordering-after-durability invariant untested everywhere (only incidental via call order).

**F5 (Low severity reliability, Medium confidence): Inherited GIT_* location environment variables are forwarded to every git invocation.**
- Evidence: gitEnvironment (publisher.go:284-302) strips only GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT/LC_ALL overrides; GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE/GIT_INDEX_FILE/GIT_COMMON_DIR/GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY pass through; -C dir doesn't override GIT_DIR.
- Bad outcome: invoking ultraplan under an env carrying GIT_DIR (git hooks, GH Actions checkout exports absolute GIT_DIR) redirects all publication git ops to the wrong repository; with execute's All:true this commits+pushes an unintended repo.
- Mitigating: relative GIT_DIR resolves post -C (often harmless); most interactive shells lack these vars; fail-closed escape checks catch many wrong-root cases except All:true.
- Fix: filter location-affecting GIT_* vars in gitEnvironment.

**Defended non-issues:**
- Whole-branch push scope (docs configuration.md:222, user-guide.md:307 document pushing current branch/upstream; retry-without-duplicate pinned by test) — documented contract, opt-in mode.
- Study run-loop halting scheduling on publication error (run_loop.go:345-347) — matches documented fail-closed semantics; state durable/resumable.
- Zero-value Result{} appended to Publications on early failure (sprint publication.go:51-54, study publication.go:24-26) — distinguishable from real entries (Repository==""&&Skipped==false); cosmetic JSON noise only. Actually hmm, should I report this as low finding? It's observable bad outcome-ish: machine consumers see phantom publication entry. But minor. I'll list as minor within F4 or as defended-non-issue with note. I'll put it as a minor finding bundled in F4? The instructions say substantive findings only; I'll mention briefly as low.
- Windows lock stub: CI linux-only, unsupported platform — non-issue.
- flock vs external git processes race — inherent advisory locking, CAS bounds damage; non-issue.
- Temp index file leak on SIGKILL — negligible.
- CombinedOutput stderr mixing into parsed stdout — speculative; footnote in F4? Leave out or one line.
